subsystems.name: Bidirectional charger
subsystems.role: converts grid AC to DC to charge the battery, and DC back to AC to feed the grid.

subsystems.name: Vehicle battery and management
subsystems.role: stores and releases energy while protecting battery health.

subsystems.name: Communication and control
subsystems.role: lets the vehicle, charger, aggregator and grid operator agree on power flows.

subsystems.name: Aggregation platform
subsystems.role: bundles many vehicles into a single controllable resource.

subsystems.name: Grid interface and protection
subsystems.role: connects safely to the local distribution network.

buildSteps.title: Design bidirectional power electronics
buildSteps.detail: The charger must handle power in both directions efficiently and safely, with isolation between vehicle and grid.

buildSteps.title: Integrate vehicle-side controls
buildSteps.detail: The BMS must accept external commands, manage state of charge limits and monitor cell temperatures during discharge.

buildSteps.title: Implement communication standards
buildSteps.detail: The vehicle, charger and back-end systems are programmed to a common protocol so they can exchange power limits and schedules.

buildSteps.title: Build the aggregation platform
buildSteps.detail: Software registers vehicles, predicts availability, and translates grid requests into charging or discharging commands.

buildSteps.title: Install grid connection and protection
buildSteps.detail: An electrician wires the charger to the local network with relays that disconnect it if the grid fails, preventing back-feed onto dead lines.

buildSteps.title: Run controlled pilots
buildSteps.detail: A fleet of vehicles is enrolled to test response times, battery wear and driver acceptance under real grid conditions.

buildSteps.title: Qualify for grid markets
buildSteps.detail: The aggregator meets the rules of frequency-response or capacity markets so it can be paid for its service.

buildSteps.title: Scale deployment
buildSteps.detail: Cheaper bidirectional chargers and standardised vehicles allow wider rollout in homes, depots and workplaces.

prerequisites.why: only some vehicle models and charger types support reverse power flow today.
protocols such as ISO 15118-20 and OCPP are still being widely implemented.
the grid must measure and manage many small, dispersed power flows.
most electricity markets are not yet fully open to small, mobile storage.
frequent cycling must be limited to avoid shortening pack life.

pathway.milestone: pilot projects and early commercial chargers demonstrating vehicle-to-grid and vehicle-to-home
pathway.unlocks: proof that batteries can support the grid without harming drivers.

pathway.milestone: standardised bidirectional vehicles and chargers on sale
aggregators competing in frequency and capacity markets
pathway.unlocks: a new revenue stream for EV owners and a flexible grid buffer.

pathway.milestone: large-scale V2G as routine grid infrastructure
pathway.unlocks: cheaper integration of variable renewables and deferred network upgrades.
